one_line_description.value: Notion's API is a REST API for building integrations, automations, and tools that read and write Notion workspace content such as pages, databases, comments, and files.
one_line_description.quote: Notion API is a REST API for building integrations, automations, and tools that read and write Notion workspace content.

api_breadth.value: REST, read-write across pages, databases/data sources, comments, files, users, and webhooks; official docs do not state a total endpoint count
api_breadth.quote: Read, create, update, and search content; read and create comments; and read supported user information through Notion's REST API.

docs_url.quote: Find the base URL, headers, and data formats for Notion API requests.

auth_methods.quote: Internal connections use a static credential called an internal connection API token, personal access tokens use a user-scoped static token, and OAuth integrations and public integrations use the OAuth 2.0 protocol.

access_model.quote: Workspace owners can always create PATs with Notion API access.

access_notes.value: Development credentials are self-serve: a user can create a personal access token (or internal connection) in the Developer portal with no paid plan required. On Free plans PAT creation is limited to workspace owners and is not configurable; on Business/Enterprise plans PAT creation is restricted by default and admins can choose workspace owners only or all members. Multi-user products should use an OAuth public integration so each user authorizes access.
access_notes.quote: | Free | Workspace owners only. | Not configurable. | | Plus | All workspace members. | Not configurable. | | Business | Workspace owners only. | Admins can choose Workspace owners only or All workspace members. |

rate_limits.value: Per-connection: 600 requests per 60s window on Business/Enterprise (avg 10/s), 180 requests per 60s on all other plans (avg 3/s); data source queries ~3 requests/s per connection; plus a separate shared per-workspace limit; 429 responses include Retry-After
rate_limits.quote: | Business and Enterprise | 600 requests per minute (an average of 10 per second) | | All other plans | 180 requests per minute (an average of 3 per second) |

webhooks.quote: Setting up webhooks to react to Notion changes (page updates, comments, database schema changes)

sdk_languages.quote: The JavaScript SDK (`@notionhq/client`) wraps the REST API.

api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.value: Versioned API: requests must send a Notion-Version header, current version 2026-03-11. A formal deprecation/sunset policy was not captured in the evidence.
api_versioning_or_deprecation_notes.quote: The API is versioned (current: `2026-03-11`) and requires authentication via personal access tokens, internal connections, or OAuth.

verdict_reason: Notion documents a public REST API with read-write coverage of pages, databases/data sources, comments, files, users, and webhooks, plus a JavaScript SDK and a vendor-hosted MCP server at https://mcp.notion.com/mcp. Credentials are self-serve: any workspace owner can create a personal access token in the Developer portal without a paid plan, and OAuth 2.0 is documented for multi-user integrations. The only friction is administrative (Free-plan PATs limited to workspace owners; Business/Enterprise PAT creation restricted by default and admin-configurable), which does not require sales contact or app review to start building.
open_questions: OAuth scopes/capability list is not captured verbatim in the evidence; confirm whether Notion publishes a documented scope/permission list for OAuth integrations.
No documented sandbox or test environment was found in the evidence; confirm whether Notion offers one or whether developers are expected to test against a real workspace.
Deprecation/sunset policy (beyond the Notion-Version header) is not captured; the versioning reference page was not included in the bundle.
No community/third-party MCP servers were found in the evidence (GitHub and MCP registry checks returned nothing); confirm whether any credible ones exist.
Total endpoint/resource count is not stated in the captured docs, so api_breadth is scope-based rather than count-based.
Whether publishing a public OAuth integration requires vendor app review was not established from the evidence.
